title-group.article-title: Real-world outcomes with sacituzumab govitecan in triple-negative metastatic breast cancer.

abstract.p: Background: sacituzumab govitecan is used for patients with triple-negative metastatic breast cancer, but real-world evidence regarding outcomes after prior therapy remains limited. We evaluated treatment effectiveness and safety in routine clinical practice. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 163 adults treated with sacituzumab govitecan at 5 oncology centers between 2021 and 2025. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival. Secondary endpoints included overall survival, treatment discontinuation, dose modification, and documented adverse events. Results: Median follow-up was 16.5 months. Median progression-free survival was 5.9 months and median overall survival was 13.8 months. Objective response was observed in 36% of evaluable patients. Dose modification occurred in 31% and treatment discontinuation because of toxicity occurred in 12%. Conclusions: In this real-world cohort, sacituzumab govitecan demonstrated clinically meaningful activity with a manageable safety profile in patients with triple-negative metastatic breast cancer. Prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings. Research Sponsor: None.
